Let $n\geq 1$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be a nonempty open set with coordinates $x^1,\ldots,x^n$, and let $\mathfrak g$ be a finite-dimensional real Lie algebra with bilinear alternating bracket $[\ ,\ ]_{\mathfrak g}$ satisfying the Jacobi identity. Let $V=V_{\bar 0}\oplus V_{\bar 1}$ be a finite-dimensional $\mathbb Z_2$-graded complex vector space, and let $\rho:\mathfrak g\to\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)$ be an even representation, meaning $\rho([X,Y]_{\mathfrak g})=\rho(X)\rho(Y)-\rho(Y)\rho(X)$ for all $X,Y\in\mathfrak g$ and each $\rho(X)$ preserves the grading of $V$. This is local Lie-algebra data; no global group, principal bundle, action functional, or quantum theory is selected here.

Choose a basis $T_a$ of $\mathfrak g$ and write $[T_b,T_c]_{\mathfrak g}=f^a{}_{bc}T_a$. A local gauge potential is a $\mathfrak g$-valued one-form $A=A_\mu^aT_a\,dx^\mu$ whose component jet generators $A_{\mu,I}^a$ are even and have ghost number zero. A matter field is a $V$-valued local field $\psi$ with each component jet generator $\psi_I^\alpha$ assigned the parity of its graded component and ghost number zero. The ghost is $c=c^aT_a$, with odd component jet generators $c_I^a$ of ghost number one. The coefficient bracket of homogeneous $\mathfrak g$-valued fields is $[X,Y]^a=f^a{}_{bc}X^bY^c$, using multiplication in the graded-commutative coefficient algebra; in particular $[c,c]^a=f^a{}_{bc}c^bc^c$ has no factor of $1/2$.

For a multi-index $I=(I_1,\ldots,I_n)\in\mathbb N^n$, let $\Phi_I$ denote the corresponding formal jet generator of a field component $\Phi$. The finite-jet local algebra $\mathcal F_U$ is $C^\infty(U)$ tensored with the polynomial algebra in its even jet generators and the exterior algebra in its odd jet generators, where each element uses only finitely many jet generators. The total derivatives $D_\mu$ act by $D_\mu f=\partial_\mu f$ on $f\in C^\infty(U)$ and $D_\mu\Phi_I=\Phi_{I+e_\mu}$ on every jet generator; the multi-index derivatives commute.

Define the degree-one BRST operator candidate $s$ on the fields by

$$sA_\mu=\partial_\mu c+[A_\mu,c],\qquad sc=-\frac12[c,c],\qquad s\psi=-\rho(c)\psi.$$

On coefficient functions set $sf=0$, and on every jet generator set $s(\Phi_I)=D_I(s\Phi)$; extend $s$ to $\mathcal F_U$ by the odd left-derivation rule $s(FG)=(sF)G+(-1)^{|F|}F(sG)$ for homogeneous $F$, where $|F|$ is total parity. The minimal sector here contains only $A,\psi,c$ and their jets. Antighosts and Nakanishi–Lautrup variables are not included; adjoining such a nonminimal pair requires separate definitions and a proof before any cohomological triviality claim. The specified data are a BRST complex once $s^2=0$, which is established for these formulas in the following nilpotence lemma.

actual_anchors.exact_section_text: Let $n\geq 1$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be nonempty and open, let $\mathfrak g$ be a finite-dimensional real Lie algebra, and let $V=V_{\bar 0}\oplus V_{\bar 1}$ be a finite-dimensional graded complex vector space with an even Lie-algebra representation $\rho:\mathfrak g\to\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)$. Form the graded-commutative finite-jet algebra over $C^\infty(U)$ from an even $\mathfrak g$-valued local one-form $A=A_\mu^aT_a\,dx^\mu$, a ghost $c=c^aT_a$ with odd components of ghost number one, and matter fields $\psi^\alpha$ of fixed component parity and ghost number zero. Let $D_\mu$ be the total derivatives on coefficient functions and formal field jets, and let $s$ be the left odd derivation of ghost number one specified by $sA_\mu=\partial_\mu c+[A_\mu,c]$, $sc=-\tfrac12[c,c]$, $s\psi=-\rho(c)\psi$, and $s(D_I\Phi)=D_I(s\Phi)$ on every multi-index jet. Then $s^2=0$ on the entire finite-jet algebra and $sD_\mu=D_\mu s$ for each $\mu$.

actual_anchors.exact_step_text: Since $c$ is odd, the coefficient bracket is graded symmetric on $(c,c)$ and $s[c,c]=2[sc,c]$. Therefore $s^2c=-\tfrac12s[c,c]=-[sc,c]=\tfrac12\lbrack\lbrack c,c\rbrack,c\rbrack$. Its component is proportional to $f^a{}_{de}f^d{}_{bc}c^bc^cc^e$; because the ghost coefficients anticommute, only the complete antisymmetrization in $b,c,e$ contributes, and the Jacobi identity $f^a{}_{d[b}f^d{}_{ce]}=0$ makes it vanish. [F1, F2, A1, algebra]

Because $A_\mu$ is even, the left-derivation rule gives $s^2A_\mu=\partial_\mu(sc)+[sA_\mu,c]+[A_\mu,sc]=-[\partial_\mu c,c]+[\partial_\mu c+[A_\mu,c],c]-\tfrac12\lbrack A_\mu,\lbrack c,c\rbrack\rbrack=\lbrack\lbrack A_\mu,c\rbrack,c\rbrack-\tfrac12\lbrack A_\mu,\lbrack c,c\rbrack\rbrack=0$. Here $\partial_\mu[c,c]=2[\partial_\mu c,c]$, and Jacobi with $A_\mu$ even and $c$ odd gives $\lbrack A_\mu,\lbrack c,c\rbrack\rbrack=2\lbrack\lbrack A_\mu,c\rbrack,c\rbrack$. [F1, F2, A1, algebra]

For any homogeneous matter component, the odd left-derivation rule gives $s^2\psi=-\rho(sc)\psi+\rho(c)s\psi=\tfrac12\rho([c,c])\psi-\rho(c)^2\psi$. Writing $c=c^aT_a$, graded commutativity yields $\rho(c)^2=\tfrac12c^ac^b[\rho(T_a),\rho(T_b)]=\tfrac12\rho([c,c])$ by [A2], so $s^2\psi=0$ for either matter parity. [F1, F2, A2, algebra]

On a coefficient function $f(x)$, both $sD_\mu f$ and $D_\mu sf$ vanish. On each jet generator $\Phi_I$, the defining rule gives $sD_\mu\Phi_I=s\Phi_{I+e_\mu}=D_\mu D_I(s\Phi)=D_\mu s\Phi_I$, since the total derivatives commute. Thus $sD_\mu=D_\mu s$ on generators, and composition gives $s^2\Phi_I=D_I(s^2\Phi)=0$ for every multi-index $I$. The square of an odd derivation is an even derivation because its two cross terms cancel, so steps 1.1–1.3 and this jet calculation make $s^2$ vanish on every finite polynomial in the generators. [F2, step 1.1, step 1.2, step 1.3] ∎

Let $n\geq1$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be nonempty and open, let $\mathcal F_U$ be the finite-jet local algebra with nilpotent BRST derivation $s$ and commuting total derivatives $D_\mu$, and let $dx^1,\ldots,dx^n$ be anticommuting coordinate one-forms. For $g\in\mathbb Z$ and $0\leq p\leq n$, let $\mathcal A_U^{g,p}$ be the space of local horizontal $p$-forms of ghost number $g$, namely finite sums of $dx^{\mu_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge dx^{\mu_p}$ with coefficients in the ghost-number-$g$ part of $\mathcal F_U$. Define the horizontal differential $d_H:=dx^\mu D_\mu$; its square is $d_H^2a=dx^\mu\wedge dx^\nu D_\mu D_\nu a=\tfrac12dx^\mu\wedge dx^\nu[D_\mu,D_\nu]a=0$. Extend $s$ to horizontal forms by $s(dx^\mu\wedge a)=-dx^\mu\wedge sa$. Since $sD_\mu=D_\mu s$, one has $s(d_Ha)=-dx^\mu\wedge D_\mu(sa)=-d_H(sa)$, hence $sd_H+d_Hs=0$.

For $p=0$, set $\mathcal A_U^{g,-1}=\{0\}$. The local BRST cohomology modulo total derivatives in bidegree $(g,p)$ is

$$H^{g,p}(s\mid d_H):=\frac{\{a\in\mathcal A_U^{g,p}:\text{there is }b\in\mathcal A_U^{g+1,p-1}\text{ with }sa+d_Hb=0\}}{\{sm+d_Hn:m\in\mathcal A_U^{g-1,p},\ n\in\mathcal A_U^{g,p-1}\}}.$$

The denominator is a subspace of the numerator: for $a=sm+d_Hn$, choose $b=sn$ and compute $sa+d_Hb=s^2m+sd_Hn+d_Hsn=0$. For $p=0$, $n=b=0$ and the same verification reduces to $s^2m=0$. This is cohomology of the specified local jet algebra and horizontal differential; it is not cohomology of a physical state space or Hilbert space. Interpreting $d_H$-exact top forms as equal local functionals additionally assumes compact support or boundary conditions that make the corresponding surface term vanish.

Use the local field data and BRST convention on an open set $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ given by a finite-dimensional real Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$, a graded representation space $V$, an even $\mathfrak g$-valued gauge potential $A_\mu$, an odd ghost $c$ of ghost number $1$, and matter components $\psi^\alpha$ of parity $\epsilon_\alpha$ and ghost number $0$. For every field or ghost coordinate $\Phi^A$ of parity $\epsilon_A$ and ghost number $g_A$, introduce an antifield $\Phi_A^*$ of parity $\epsilon_A+1\pmod 2$ and ghost number $-1-g_A$. Thus $A^*$ and the antifields of even matter are odd of ghost number $-1$, while $c^*$ is even of ghost number $-2$. The minimal sector consists of $A,\psi,c$ and these antifields.

For a finite-dimensional canonical coordinate algebra, take the polynomial algebra in the even coordinates tensor the exterior algebra in the odd coordinates. In the local-field notation, use finite-jet local functionals with variational derivatives only when the chosen domain makes those derivatives and integrations by parts well-defined; compact support or boundary conditions that kill surface terms are part of that domain. For homogeneous functionals $F,G$, define the canonical antibracket by

$$
(F,G):=\sum_A\left(\frac{\partial_r F}{\partial\Phi^A}\frac{\partial_lG}{\partial\Phi_A^*}-\frac{\partial_rF}{\partial\Phi_A^*}\frac{\partial_lG}{\partial\Phi^A}\right),
$$

with an integral over $U$ replacing the sum in a local-field expression. Left and right derivatives are the graded derivatives acting from the indicated side. This convention has odd parity, ghost number $+1$, the shifted graded-skew identity, the shifted Jacobi identity, and the graded Leibniz identity. A regular finite-dimensional canonical domain has no nonzero central element of ghost number $1$: an element central against every coordinate has all coordinate derivatives zero and is a numerical constant. A formal local-functional domain used below must separately satisfy this same no-ghost-number-one-center condition.

Let a local gauge parameter be a smooth map $\lambda:U\to\mathfrak g$, and define its infinitesimal action on the fields by $\delta_\lambda A_\mu=\partial_\mu\lambda+[A_\mu,\lambda]$ and $\delta_\lambda\psi=-\rho(\lambda)\psi$. Write these variations as $\delta_\lambda\Phi^i=R^i_\alpha[\Phi]\lambda^\alpha$, where $R$ is the resulting linear differential operator in $\lambda$. Assume this declared gauge action is irreducible: if $\delta_\lambda\Phi^i\equiv0$ for every field configuration, then $\lambda\equiv0$. Assume also that its Lie-algebra action closes off shell, meaning its commutator closes without using equations of motion, and that no additional gauge symmetry is included. Let $S_0[A,\psi]$ be a specified local classical action invariant under these transformations. Write $s_0$ for the BRST operator on the minimal fields given by $s_0A_\mu=\partial_\mu c+[A_\mu,c]$, $s_0c=-\tfrac12[c,c]$, and $s_0\psi=-\rho(c)\psi$. The minimal BV functional candidate is

$$S_{\mathrm{BV}}:=S_0+\int_U d^nx\,\sum_A(-1)^{\epsilon_A}\Phi_A^*\,s_0\Phi^A,$$

Let $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ have basis $T_a$ with $[T_b,T_c]=\epsilon^a{}_{bc}T_a$. Form the finite graded-commutative coordinate algebra $\mathcal B=\mathbb C[c_1^*,c_2^*,c_3^*]\otimes\Lambda(c^1,c^2,c^3)$, where each $c^a$ is odd of ghost number $1$ and each $c_a^*$ is even of ghost number $-2$. Use the canonical antibracket

$$
(F,G)=\sum_{a=1}^3\left(\frac{\partial_rF}{\partial c^a}\frac{\partial_lG}{\partial c_a^*}-\frac{\partial_rF}{\partial c_a^*}\frac{\partial_lG}{\partial c^a}\right).
$$

For $S_{\mathrm{CE}}=\tfrac12c_a^*\epsilon^a{}_{bc}c^bc^c$, the element $S_{\mathrm{CE}}$ is even with ghost number zero and satisfies $(S_{\mathrm{CE}},S_{\mathrm{CE}})=0$. Hence the Hamiltonian differential $sF=(S_{\mathrm{CE}},F)$ is nilpotent. This is only the finite-dimensional non-Abelian ghost sector; it is not a Yang–Mills action or a quantum field theory.

actual_anchors.exact_step_text: The ghost number of $S_{\mathrm{CE}}$ is $-2+1+1=0$, and its parity is even. The derivative convention gives $\partial_rS_{\mathrm{CE}}/\partial c^a=-c_e^*\epsilon^e{}_{ab}c^b$, $\partial_lS_{\mathrm{CE}}/\partial c^a=+c_e^*\epsilon^e{}_{ab}c^b$, and $\partial_rS_{\mathrm{CE}}/\partial c_a^*=\partial_lS_{\mathrm{CE}}/\partial c_a^*=\tfrac12\epsilon^a{}_{cd}c^cc^d$. Since $c_a^*$ is even, substitution in the defining bracket gives $(S_{\mathrm{CE}},S_{\mathrm{CE}})=(-c_e^*\epsilon^e{}_{ab}c^b)(\tfrac12\epsilon^a{}_{cd}c^cc^d)-(\tfrac12\epsilon^a{}_{cd}c^cc^d)(+c_e^*\epsilon^e{}_{ab}c^b)=-c_e^*\epsilon^e{}_{ab}\epsilon^a{}_{cd}c^bc^cc^d$. The ghost product is totally antisymmetric, so the tensor contraction reduces to its antisymmetrization $\epsilon^e{}_{a[b}\epsilon^a{}_{cd]}$, which is the Jacobi identity and vanishes by [A1]. [A1, F1, algebra]

The coordinate algebra is finite and canonical, so its center consists of constants and has no nonzero ghost-number-one element. Step 1.1 proves the classical master equation, and [F2] therefore gives $s^2=0$ on the entire algebra. [F2, step 1.1] ∎

actual_anchors.exact_section_text: Assume full AC. Let $M$ be a finite-dimensional complex manifold, let $\mathcal F$ be a coherent analytic $\mathcal O_M$-module, and let $V$ be a nonempty open subset of one holomorphic chart on which a finite presentation $\mathcal O_V^{p_1}\to\mathcal O_V^{p_0}\xrightarrow{\pi}\mathcal F|_V\to0$ is fixed. Assume that the induced section map $\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V^{p_0})\to\Gamma(V,\mathcal F)$ is surjective. Then its quotient topology from compact-convergence on $\mathcal O(V)^{p_0}$ is a Fréchet topology. If two such presentations are locally defined on a common cover and both section maps are surjective, their quotient topologies agree; the compatible-family topology on sections over any open set admitting a countable cover by such presentation neighborhoods is also Fréchet and independent of the chosen chart cover and presentations.

actual_anchors.exact_step_text: Let two finite presentations be given near a point $x$, with coherent relation kernels $K,K'$ by [A2]. Apply [A3] to both kernels and intersect the resulting polydisc neighborhoods with the presentation neighborhoods. On a sufficiently small coordinate polydisc $D$ in this intersection, $H^1(D,K)=H^1(D,K')=0$. The long exact sequence [F5] for each presentation then proves that both section maps on $D$ are surjective. More generally, on any common open set $W$ where both presentations are defined and their section maps are surjective, lift the images of the finitely many basis sections of the first free module through the second section surjection. These lifts form a holomorphic matrix $A$ on $W$ with $\pi'A=\pi$. Multiplication by $A$ is continuous for compact-convergence because its entries are bounded on compact subsets; it induces the identity continuously between the quotient topologies. Reversing the presentations gives the reverse continuous identity. Thus the quotient topologies agree on each common presentation neighborhood. A holomorphic change of chart preserves compact-convergence because it and its inverse send compact subsets to compact subsets. [A1, A2, A3, F1, F5, step 1.1, step 2.1, given, construct]

First consider a presentation neighborhood $V$ with its surjective section map and quotient topology. If a small chart polydisc $D\subseteq V$ has a target presentation whose section map is surjective, the restricted images of the finitely many source free generators lift to target free sections on $D$. As in step 3.1, these lifts give a holomorphic matrix on $D$. Restricting source free sections and multiplying by that matrix is continuous for compact-convergence, so passage through the two quotient maps proves continuity of $\Gamma(V,\mathcal F)\to\Gamma(D,\mathcal F)$. For any countable cover $(V_i)$ by such presentation neighborhoods, choose countably many sufficiently small polydiscs $D_{ij\nu}$ covering every overlap $V_i\cap V_j$, with surjective local section maps as in step 3.1. The restrictions from each $V_i,V_j$ into each such polydisc are continuous by the matrix argument. Therefore the compatible families are the intersection of the kernels of the continuous differences into $\Gamma(D_{ij\nu},\mathcal F)$. Those targets are Hausdorff Fréchet spaces by step 2.1, so this intersection is closed in the countable product of the local section spaces. A countable product of Fréchet spaces is Fréchet by enumerating their seminorms and taking componentwise limits; a closed subspace is complete for its restricted metric. Thus the compatible-family space is an actual Fréchet space. Compatibility checked on these overlap covers is full compatibility by the sheaf axiom. [A1, F4, F7, step 2.1, step 3.1, construct]

To compare the quotient topology on an arbitrary presentation neighborhood $V$ with its topology from local sections, cover $V$ by countably many sufficiently small presentation polydiscs $(D_\nu)$ as in step 3.1. The restriction map from the already Fréchet quotient $\Gamma(V,\mathcal F)$ into the compatible-family space for this cover is continuous by step 4.1. It is a linear bijection by unique sheaf gluing. Both its source and target are Fréchet by step 2.1 and step 4.1, so [F6] makes it a topological isomorphism. In particular, inverse gluing is continuous, and the original arbitrary-$V$ presentation quotient agrees with the compatible-family topology; no unproved identification of these topologies is made. [F4, F6, F7, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, construct]

Any two countable presentation covers have a common countable refinement by sufficiently small presentation polydiscs; choose them inside the local vanishing neighborhoods of the finitely many relation kernels involved at each source-target comparison, as in step 3.1. Restriction from either compatible-family space into the refined compatible-family space is continuous by the local matrix argument of step 4.1 and is a bijection by sheaf gluing. All these spaces are Fréchet by step 4.1, so [F6] makes both maps topological isomorphisms. The identity on ordinary sections therefore identifies the two cover topologies. Together with the presentation and chart comparison in step 3.1 and the quotient-to-family comparison in step 5.1, this proves every asserted independence. [A1, F4, F6, F7, step 3.1, step 4.1, step 5.1, construct] ∎

Let $\mathbb C^*=\mathbb C\setminus\{0\}$. For every holomorphic function $f\in\mathcal O(\mathbb C^*)$, there are unique entire functions $g,h\in\mathcal O(\mathbb C)$ and a unique scalar $a\in\mathbb C$ such that
$$
f(z)=g(z)+a z^{-1}+z^{-2}h(1/z)\qquad(z\in\mathbb C^*).
$$

actual_anchors.exact_step_text: By [F1], write $f(z)=\sum_{n\in\mathbb Z}c_nz^n$ on $\mathbb C^*$, with both one-sided series uniformly convergent on every compact subannulus. Fix $R>0$ and integrate the uniformly convergent series on the positively oriented circle $\gamma_R(t)=Re^{it}$ after multiplying by $z^{-n-1}$. By [F2], termwise integration is valid, and direct parametrization gives $(2\pi i)^{-1}\int_{\gamma_R}z^{k-n-1}\,dz=1$ for $k=n$ and $0$ otherwise. Thus $$ c_n=\frac1{2\pi i}\int_{\gamma_R}f(z)z^{-n-1}\,dz $$ for every $n\in\mathbb Z$ and every $R>0$. [F1, F2, given, construct]

Define $g(z)=\sum_{n\ge0}c_nz^n$. For any $S>0$, choose $R>S$; on $|z|\le S$ the terms satisfy $|c_nz^n|\le M_R(S/R)^n$ by step 2.1, so the series converges uniformly there. Its partial sums are polynomials, hence [F3] makes $g$ entire. [F3, step 2.1, construct]

Define $h(w)=\sum_{j\ge0}c_{-(j+2)}w^j$. Given $S>0$, choose $0<R<1/S$; on $|w|\le S$ the terms satisfy $|c_{-(j+2)}w^j|\le M_RR^2(RS)^j$ by step 2.1, so this series also converges uniformly on every closed disk.
